spans.s:
Baka Dālbhya (‘descendant of Dalbha’) is the name of a
person mentioned in the Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa as
constraining Indra for the Ājakeśins (i. 9, 2), and as a Kuru-
Pañcāla (iv. 7, 2).

Bakura is mentioned in one passage of the Rigveda,^1 where
it is said that the Aśvins made light for the Āryan by blowing
their Bakura against the Dasyus. According to the Nirukta,^2
the thunderbolt^1 is meant; but much more probable is Roth's^3
view, that the object blown was a musical instrument. See
also

Bākura in one passage of the Rigveda (ix. 1, 8) is used as
an epithet of Dṛti, the combined words denoting a wind
instrument of some kind. Cf. Bakura.
